claims.text: Enhanced free-energy sampling calibrated with high-temperature in-situ neutron imaging can accurately determine melting temperature.
The proposed approach can accurately determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The proposed approach can accurately determine volume change at melting.
The proposed approach can accurately determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
The approach applies across a broad and diverse range of high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The applicable initial material is a well-mixed, single-phase solid-solution HEA near its melting point.
Equilibrium high-temperature conditions close to the melting transition are required.
Sufficient differences in neutron transmission among elements are necessary to obtain useful phase contrast.
A free-energy landscape connects the solid and liquid phases during melting.
Enhanced sampling overcomes energy barriers associated with the solid-to-liquid transition.
Enhanced sampling enables calculation of solid-liquid free-energy differences.
High-temperature in-situ neutron imaging can visually capture melting, liquid phase separation, and remixing in HEA-related alloys.
Neutron-imaging observations can be used to calibrate simulated free-energy profiles.
Such calibration increases the accuracy and efficiency of extracting melting-related thermodynamic parameters.
Predicted melting and fusion parameters will agree with independent measurements within approximately 5–10% across diverse HEAs.
Traditional calorimetry and DSC lack the efficiency needed to screen a wide HEA compositional space.
Standard molecular dynamics cannot capture all melting-related properties simultaneously with high precision.
Complex multiphase transitions may limit the method's reliability.
Low elemental neutron contrast limits the reliability or applicability of neutron imaging.
Consistent deviations greater than approximately 10% across multiple HEA compositions would falsify the proposed approach.
